cases.original_forecast: Base favours NH3; subsequent acid returns nitrogen toward ammonium and lowers its gas-phase share without removing total nitrogen.

original_checks.criterion: Track NH3 gas separately from ammonium and dissolved ammonia.
Nitrogen is conserved through the closed acid–base cycle.

original_limitations: Neutralisation heat affects pressure; gas-species accounting is essential.

cases.original_forecast: Captured carbonate carbon should remain with the isolated solid and reappear as CO2/dissolved carbon on acidification; uncaptured carbon stays in the earlier liquid/gas accounts.

original_checks.criterion: Quantify carbon in the first solid before assigning recaptured gas to it.
Sum carbon over both vessels and any boundary transfer during filtration.

original_limitations: Filtration and resealing may alter headspace inventory; the carbon ledger, not pressure alone, establishes recovery.

cases.original_forecast: The catalyst-free filtrate should consume less additional peroxide than the unfiltered control, after correcting for their inventories at filtration.

original_checks.criterion: Record the post-filtration starting peroxide in v3.
Distinguish slowed uncatalysed reaction from a claim of absolutely zero decomposition.

original_limitations: Any catalyst transfer or dissolved catalytic species would confound ideal physical removal.

cases.original_forecast: A lower aqueous fraction, an organic liquid fraction and an insoluble solid residue should be distinguishable, subject to the operators’ actual phase semantics.

original_checks.criterion: Identify the composition of each destination rather than assigning it from vessel number.
Close water, hexane, salt and silica balances across all three vessels.

original_limitations: Interfacial trapping, emulsions and solid entrainment may be outside the ideal model.

cases.original_forecast: Both mixtures can neutralise approximately 0.0005 mol of hydroxide, so the neutralisation contribution should be similar rather than doubled. The second mixture retains more excess acid.

original_checks.criterion: Calculate temperature changes against each pair of measured pre-mixing temperatures and heat capacities.
Confirm the same hydroxide consumption but different residual acidity.

original_limitations: Dilution heat and different initial solution temperatures can affect raw temperature rises; raw final temperatures are not reaction heats.

metrics.thermal_interpretation: Integrate actual premixing inventory Cp to actual finalT; subtract sensible mixing and retain earlier excess/dissolution ledgers separately. Existing calorimeter energy is not newly generated neutralisation heat. No exactfourfold or empiricalenthalpyclaim.

cases.original_forecast: Both arms can neutralise 0.001 mol, but the less dilute arm should show the larger mixing-corrected temperature rise because it has a smaller thermal mass.

original_checks.criterion: Compare heat-capacity-weighted pre-mixing baselines with final temperatures.
Distinguish approximately equal neutralisation energy from unequal temperature changes; do not demand an exact fourfold ratio.

original_limitations: Different concentrations introduce activity and dilution-enthalpy effects; total solution heat capacities are not exactly proportional to water volume.

metrics.thermal_interpretation: Integrate actual premixing inventory Cp to actual finalT; subtract sensible mixing and retain earlier excess/dissolution ledgers separately. Existing calorimeter energy is not newly generated neutralisation heat. No exactfourfold or empiricalenthalpyclaim.

qualification: Bounded original criteria, complete owned material/phase accounting and explicit diagnostic limits; no experimental calibration.
